blocks.label: Pre-mid vs post-mid
blocks.text: Pre-mid = everything up to **information gain in decision trees**. Everything after that, including decision-tree overfitting, kNN and LWR, is post-mid. Across all four papers (160 marks) the split is **15% / 85%**.

blocks.label: How to use this paper
blocks.text: Open **Worked problems** and try each question on paper before revealing the steps.

problem.text: Three hypotheses with P(h1|D) = 0.5, P(h2|D) = 0.3, P(h3|D) = 0.2. For a new candidate, h1 predicts **win**; h2 and h3 predict **lose**. What is the most probable classification?

steps.label: Idea
steps.text: The Bayes optimal classifier weights each hypothesis's vote by its posterior: P(v|D) = Σ P(v|hᵢ)·P(hᵢ|D).

steps.label: Conclusion
steps.text: Both are 0.5, so win and lose are **equally probable** (a tie). Note the MAP hypothesis h1 alone would have said *win*: this is the classic example where Bayes optimal and MAP disagree.

problem.text: Positive points: x = 1, 3, 5. Negative points: x = 0, 2, 4, 6 (all on the x-axis). Use the kernel trick to find a separating hyperplane with a non-linear SVM. Plot before and after the transformation.

steps.label: Before
steps.text: On the line the labels alternate − + − + − + −, so no single threshold separates them: **not linearly separable**.

steps.label: Transform
steps.text: Use φ(x) = x mod 2 (odd → 1, even → 0). Positives map to 1, negatives map to 0. Plot each point as (x, φ(x)): positives sit at height 1, negatives at height 0.

steps.label: Hyperplane
steps.text: In the new space the classes are separated by the horizontal line **y = 0.5**, halfway between the two levels (maximum margin).

steps.label: Marks
steps.text: 3 marks for the transformation, 2 for the hyperplane. Any transform that sends odds and evens to different values (e.g. cos(πx)) also works.

worked.title: Q3 · EM with one Gaussian (7 marks)

problem.text: Data: −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Fit a Gaussian mixture with exactly **one** Gaussian using EM. Initial mean 10, initial variance 1.

steps.label: E-step
steps.text: With one component π₁ = 1, so every responsibility γ(zₙ₁) = π₁N(xₙ)/π₁N(xₙ) = **1**, whatever the starting mean.

steps.label: N₁
steps.text: N₁ = Σγ = 9, the number of points.

steps.label: Convergence
steps.text: The next E-step again gives all γ = 1, so the M-step returns the same μ and σ². EM has **converged after one iteration**: the answer is simply the sample mean and the (divide-by-N) variance.

worked.answer: μ = 0, σ² = 60/9 ≈ 6.67; converges in one iteration.

worked.title: Q4 · MLE of a coin (5 marks)

problem.text: 100 tosses of the same coin: 30 heads, 70 tails. p = P(head). How many 100-toss datasets have the same likelihood as this one? Find the MLE of p.

steps.label: Likelihood
steps.text: P(D|p) = p³⁰(1−p)⁷⁰. It depends only on the counts, not the order.

steps.label: Same likelihood
steps.text: Any sequence with exactly 30 heads has the same likelihood. Choose 30 of the 100 positions for the heads: **¹⁰⁰C₃₀ = 100! / (30!·70!)** datasets.

steps.label: Log-likelihood
steps.text: log L = 30 log p + 70 log(1−p)

worked.title: Q5 · XOR data and a closed-form network (5 marks)

problem.text: Points: (−1,−1) +, (−1,1) −, (1,−1) −, (1,1) +. (a) Comment on separability. (b) Give a 1-D transformation that is linearly separable and one that is not. (c) A network has two hidden layers of two units each, all weights 1. The top unit of each layer uses sigmoid and the bottom one tanh; the output is ReLU of the sum of its two inputs. Write the output in closed form.

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: This is **XOR**: the positives are on one diagonal and the negatives on the other. No straight line separates them, so the data is **not linearly separable**.

steps.label: (b) separable
steps.text: z = x₁·x₂ gives +1 for both positives and −1 for both negatives. A threshold at z = 0 separates them.

steps.label: (b) not separable
steps.text: z = x₁ + x₂ gives −2 and +2 for the positives but 0 and 0 for the negatives. The negatives sit between the positives, so one threshold cannot separate them.

steps.label: (c) Layer 1
steps.text: Both units get s = x₁ + x₂: h₁ = σ(x₁+x₂), h₂ = tanh(x₁+x₂).

steps.label: (c) Layer 2
steps.text: Both units get h₁ + h₂: h₃ = σ(h₁ + h₂), h₄ = tanh(h₁ + h₂).

steps.label: (c) Output
steps.text: **y = max{0, σ(σ(x₁+x₂) + tanh(x₁+x₂)) + tanh(σ(x₁+x₂) + tanh(x₁+x₂))}**

worked.answer: XOR, not linearly separable; x₁x₂ separates, x₁+x₂ does not; y = ReLU(σ(h₁+h₂) + tanh(h₁+h₂)) with h₁ = σ(x₁+x₂), h₂ = tanh(x₁+x₂).

worked.title: Q6 · Linear SVM by hand (5 marks)

problem.text: Positive: (3,2), (4,3), (2,3), (3,−1). Negative: (1,0), (−1,−1), (0,2), (−1,2). (A) Find the support vectors and the hyperplane. (B) Does the hyperplane change if (a) (2,3) is removed, (b) (5,4) is added?

steps.label: Pick the SVs
steps.text: The closest opposite-class points are **(2,3)** and **(3,−1)** (positive) and **(1,0)** (negative).

steps.label: Direction of w
steps.text: Both positive SVs lie on wᵀx + b = 1, so w ⟂ (2,3) − (3,−1) = (−1,4). Take w = a(4,1).

steps.label: Check all points
steps.text: f = (8x₁ + 2x₂ − 15)/7: positives give 13/7, 23/7, 1, 1 (all ≥ 1); negatives give −1, −25/7, −11/7, −19/7 (all ≤ −1). Feasible.

steps.label: Check optimality
steps.text: Solve α₁(2,3) + α₂(3,−1) − α₃(1,0) = w with α₁ + α₂ = α₃: α₁ = 12/49, α₂ = 22/49, α₃ = 34/49. All positive, so the KKT conditions hold and this is the maximum-margin solution.

steps.label: (B)(a) remove (2,3)
steps.text: It was a support vector, so the hyperplane **changes**. With (3,2), (3,−1) and (1,0) as the new SVs: w = (1,0), b = −2, so the new boundary is **x₁ = 2**, margin 2 (α = 1/3, 1/6, 1/2, all positive).

steps.label: (B)(b) add (5,4)
steps.text: f(5,4) = (40 + 8 − 15)/7 = 33/7 > 1: it lies outside the margin on the correct side, so it is not a support vector and the hyperplane **does not change**.

worked.answer: SVs (2,3), (3,−1), (1,0); 8x₁ + 2x₂ − 15 = 0. Removing (2,3) gives x₁ = 2; adding (5,4) changes nothing.

problem.text: Four + points at the corners of a square with one − point in the centre. Train AdaBoost with decision stumps, circle the points whose weights go up after each iteration, and run until training error is zero. (The paper gives only a picture. The working below assumes + at (0,0), (0,2), (2,0), (2,2) and − at (1,1).)

steps.label: Round 1
steps.text: No single stump isolates the centre point. Best stump: predict + everywhere. Misclassified: the **centre −**. ε₁ = 1/5, α₁ = ½ ln 4 = 0.693. Circle the − point; its weight rises to 0.5 and each + falls to 0.125.

steps.label: Round 2
steps.text: Stump x₁ < 1: + on the left, − on the right. Misclassified: **(2,0) and (2,2)**, ε₂ = 0.25, α₂ = ½ ln 3 = 0.549. Circle those two.

steps.label: Round 3
steps.text: Stump x₁ < 1.5: − on the left, + on the right. Misclassified: **(0,0) and (0,2)**, ε₃ = 1/6, α₃ = ½ ln 5 = 0.805.

steps.label: Final vote
steps.text: Centre: +0.693 − 0.549 − 0.805 < 0 ⇒ − ✓. Left corners: +0.693 + 0.549 − 0.805 > 0 ⇒ + ✓. Right corners: +0.693 − 0.549 + 0.805 > 0 ⇒ + ✓. **Zero training error after 3 iterations**.

worked.title: Q8 · K-means and initialisation (7 marks)

problem.text: Points (x₁, x₂): (−1,2), (−1,1), (−1,−1), (−1,−2), (0,0), (4,2), (4,−2). The true clusters are the first five and the last two. Run K-means with k = 2 from (A) C1 = (−1,2), C2 = (0,0) and (B) C1 = (−0.5,0), C2 = (0,0). Comment on each result and on the drawback it shows.

steps.label: (A) iteration 2
steps.text: The assignments do not change, so it has **converged**: {(−1,2), (−1,1)} and the other five. This does **not** match the true clusters.

steps.label: (B) iteration 1
steps.text: Distances to (−0.5,0) vs (0,0): the four x₁ = −1 points go to C1, while (0,0), (4,2), (4,−2) go to C2. New centres: C1 = (−1, 0), C2 = (8/3, 0) ≈ (2.67, 0).

steps.label: (B) iteration 2
steps.text: (0,0) is now 1 from C1 and 2.67 from C2, so it moves to C1. New centres: C1 = (−0.8, 0), C2 = (4, 0).

steps.label: (B) iteration 3
steps.text: No change, so it has converged: {the five left points} and {(4,2), (4,−2)}. This **matches** the true clusters.

steps.label: Drawback
steps.text: K-means is **sensitive to the initial centres**: different starts converge to different (sometimes wrong) local optima.

worked.answer: (A) wrong clusters after 2 iterations; (B) correct clusters after 3; K-means depends on initialisation.
